correctness.rationale: The cyclic incidence model has exactly one common line per pair of points, so there is no 4-cycle. The symmetric difference of matchings is a disjoint union of even alternating cycles. Having four shared edges leaves six in the difference and is therefore equivalent to one hexagon flip. A read-only independent reconstruction backtracked all 24 matchings, used overlap-four adjacency, checked all 576 entries against the frozen matrix and supplied bijection, and reproduced every rooted distance, intersection number, and the eight antipodal classes with one neighbor in each other class. Three pairwise disjoint matchings use all 21 edges, and every one-factorization gives such a triple. For a public reference independent of the inaccessible cited matrix endpoint, I also reconstructed Dejter's Klein graph from the 24 oriented cycles in Theorem 2, Section 3's pairing of oppositely oriented 2-arcs, and Corollary 4. An explicit computed bijection preserves all adjacency entries between this historical construction and the reconstructed flip graph. Replay: python3 /workspace/replay_checks.py 4. The count eight is of unordered partitions, not labeled edge colorings.
